newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares dip at noon in cautious mood.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares dip at noon in cautious mood.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index inched lower at midday on Thursday on an extended correction created in part by caution over 1997 interim results of listed firms, brokers said.
The index shed 0.28 points or 0.21 percent to 132.45 on thin turnover of HK$14.7 million.
The domestic A share index edged up 1.90 points or 0.46 percent to 411.49 points due to institutional buying, brokers said.
Turnover in the A share market was a modest 2.7 billion yuan.
"Investors turned wary about interim results," an analyst with China Guotai Securities said. "They are afraid of stepping on landmines."
People refrained from active buying because they expected some companies to issue disappointing earnings during the 1997 interim reporting season which would end on August 31.
A commentary in Shanghai's Business News on Wednesday said Chinese investors should be wary of interims because they were unaudited and did not represent a full year's performance.
"Technically speaking, B shares are in the correction phase," the Guotai analyst said.
Analysts said they expected the B share index to continue narrow-range movement in the afternoon.
In the B share market, conglomerate Shenzhen Zhonghao (Group) Co Ltd was the weakest performer, dropping HK$0.19 or 7.34 percent to HK$2.40.

Newcomer Beijing Yanjing Brewery Co Ltd, which listed 72 million A shares on Wednesday, surged 1.52 yuan to its 10 percent limit-up at 16.72 yuan. Volume reached 18 million shares, making it the most actively traded stock.
Brokers said investors snapped up Yanjing, China's biggest brewery, as they were optimistic about the firm's prospects.
